sources.title: Formalizing Mason-Stothers Theorem and its Corollaries in Lean 4
sources.enterprise_use: Provides a current Lean 4 formalization and an explicit elementary proof decomposition used by P025 to separate multiplicity residual, common Wronskian witness, and witness-degree capacity.
sources.not_claimed: The Mason-Stothers theorem, polynomial radical, derivative divisibility, Wronskian identities, and their formalizations are established prior mathematics and are not Enterprise Math inventions.

sources.title: Arithmetic derivatives through geometry of numbers
sources.enterprise_use: Establishes the decisive prior-art boundary for P025: arithmetic derivations can be constrained to a chosen equation a+b=c, satisfy a Leibniz rule, admit controlled-size existence results, and yield a small-derivative formulation tightly equivalent to abc. P025 reinterprets this as a relation-conditioned witness-family pressure test rather than claiming an integer Mason derivative as new.
sources.not_claimed: Arithmetic derivations adapted to a+b=c, their geometry-of-numbers construction, the arithmetic Wronskian bounds, and the Small Derivatives Conjecture/abc equivalence are Pasten's prior work and are not Enterprise Math inventions.

sources.title: Bounds on the exceptional set in the abc conjecture
sources.enterprise_use: Provides a modern power-saving exceptional-set result for abc-type failures. P025 uses it only as prior art for the idea that a non-exact collapse can still have quantitatively sparse bad states.
sources.not_claimed: The exceptional-set estimates, determinant/geometry/Fourier methods, and power-saving results are external analytic number theory and are not Enterprise Math inventions.

sources.title: On the exceptional set in the abc conjecture
sources.enterprise_use: Provides the explicit O(X^(56/85+epsilon)) exceptional-set exponent used by P025 as a current quantitative benchmark for sparse failure.
sources.not_claimed: The 56/85 exponent and its analytic optimization are Li's result and are not Enterprise Math inventions.

sources.title: Generalization of the ABC theorem on locally nilpotent derivations
sources.enterprise_use: Marks the broader prior-art neighborhood for derivation-based ABC generalization, preventing P025 from claiming that abstracting Mason-Stothers through derivations is itself novel.
sources.not_claimed: ABC-type results formulated with locally nilpotent derivations and the associated algebraic applications are established external work and are not Enterprise Math inventions.
